_levels: nogo = not allowed or don't go; high = serious risk, go only prepared and informed; caution = check before you go

wild-ice: Natural ice, nobody measures it. Needs at least 4 in of clear hard ice per person (white ice ~2x); test as you go with a pole or auger, carry ice picks and a throw rope, never alone.
lake-ski: Lake crossings: snow insulates and hides weak ice and overflow (slush under the snow). Stay on established tracks across the lake.

ice-lake-hood: Closed to pedestrians year-round: active seaplane / ski-plane base. Walking or skating on the ice is not permitted.
ice-lake-spenard: Part of the Lake Hood seaplane base: active aircraft operations on the ice. Airport guidance: stay off the ice.
ice-portage: Unmonitored ice over a 600-ft-deep lake; slow to freeze and often not safe in late December. Pressure ridges, leads, refrozen open water.
Calving sends waves under the ice (two skaters were stranded and helicopter-rescued in Feb 2025). Stay far back from the glacier face and off icebergs.
Avalanche and rockfall from the side slopes. No cell service. Ice reports: USFS Glacier Ranger District 907-783-3242.
portage-lake: Lake ice is unmonitored and often not yet safe in late December; ask the USFS ranger district (907-783-3242) before walking out.
Keep well back from the calving glacier face.
byron: Trail runs through avalanche runout under steep walls; the Forest Service and the Chugach avalanche center advise against winter travel without avalanche gear and training. Never enter the 'ice caves' (collapsing avalanche debris).
flattop: The winter summit gully is icy and avalanche-prone, with past fatalities. Turn around at Blueberry Knoll or the saddle unless experienced; microspikes. Check cnfaic.org.
Glen Alps Road is steep and icy.
ski-turnagain-pass: Serious avalanche terrain, ungroomed. Read the Chugach avalanche forecast (cnfaic.org) and carry beacon, probe, shovel and training.
ski-powerline-pass: The upper valley below the pass is avalanche terrain; the lower valley is gentle. Check cnfaic.org (Chugach State Park) before going past the first few miles.
ski-rabbit-lake: Bowl below the Suicide Peaks: avalanche terrain. Canyon Road is rough (4WD).
ice-rabbit-lake: Alpine bowl in avalanche terrain; by late December usually snowed over. Check cnfaic.org.
ice-eagle-symphony: ~5 mi in through avalanche terrain; usually snowed over by late December.
ski-archangel: Valley road lined by avalanche paths. Check the Hatcher Pass Avalanche Center (hpavalanche.org).
ski-independence-mine: Avalanche terrain directly above the groomed area; stay on the trails and check hpavalanche.org.
Hatcher Pass road: steep, icy, plowed only to the lower lots; 4WD and snow tyres advised. Grooming permit uncertain this season.
hatcher: Steep avalanche terrain everywhere off the road. Check hpavalanche.org and 511.alaska.gov.
Road can be icy and closed after storms; colder and windier than Anchorage.
ski-johnson-pass: Easy valley touring at first, but avalanche paths farther in. Check cnfaic.org.
ski-bird-valley: Crosses the Penguin Peak avalanche path: cross quickly, one at a time. Watch for creek overflow.
ski-indian-valley: Upper valley toward Powerline Pass is avalanche terrain; mid-winter means trail breaking.
ski-ernc: Mountain-valley touring: avalanche paths reach the trail in places. Ask at the nature center.
ski-resurrection-north: Long backcountry route with avalanche exposure in places; confirm motorized/non-motorized year with the Seward Ranger District.
ski-eklutna: Lake ice is unreliable: stay on the shoreline trail. Shared with snowmachines; side valleys are avalanche terrain; no cell signal.
eklutna: Lake ice is unmonitored; stay on the trail. Very windy and cold at the lake; side valleys are avalanche terrain.
Eklutna Lake Road (10 mi) is winding and icy.
ice-eklutna: Huge lake that freezes out of step with others; wind can open or roughen it, and a warm spell once thinned the ice to under 1 in. Check recent reports.
ice-potter: Very variable ice with open holes from marsh gas; inflow channels stay thin.
ice-twentymile: Thin ice in the passageways, gas holes throughout, wind-blown silt; Turnagain Arm swings from chinook rain to deep cold.
ice-placer: Tidal-influenced lagoons: silt, wind and uneven ice.
ice-coastal-refuge: Extreme tides and thin, inconsistent sea ice; stay close to shore. Salt and silt dull blades.
ice-jim-creek: Creek and the braided glacial Knik River are moving water: the highest break-through risk of any spot here.
ice-rabbit-slough: Overflow, very variable thickness and glacial silt in the channels; often wind-scoured, so one of the better late-December bets.
ice-big-lake: High-speed snowmachine traffic on the ice; pressure ridges.
ice-finger: Busy ice-fishing lake: watch for auger holes.
ice-matanuska-lakes: Heavily ice-fished: watch for auger holes.
ice-skilak: Very large lake with leads and pressure ridges; outside the 2-hour range.
ice-westchester: Only groomed once the ice is 12 in; inflow and outflow never freeze, so stay inside the groomed area. Late-December opening varies year to year.
ice-cheney: Maintained only once the ice is 12 in; recurring overflow.
ice-goose: Opens later in the season; the city grooms the trail around it but not always the lake.
ice-jewel: City lists it as ice-fishing only: no maintained skating.
ice-delong: City lists it as ice-fishing only: no maintained skating.
ice-beach-lake: The lake is for ice fishing only and isn't maintained for skating; ski the trails.
ski-edmonds-mirror: Lake skiing: only once the ice is safe.
ski-glen-alps: Steep, icy access road; the lot fills on clear days. Above the groomed area is avalanche terrain.
ski-coastal-trail: Exposed to wind off Cook Inlet; coastal snow is often thin or icy. Multi-use: walkers, bikes and dogs.
ski-girdwood-moose-meadows: Rain-on-snow and running water can stop grooming; check the Girdwood Nordic report.
thunderbird: Packed, icy trail: microspikes essential. The side path down to the creek is steep and slick.
beluga-point: Seward Highway: wind, ice, avalanche-control closures and a bad crash record. Drive in daylight, headlights on, check 511.alaska.gov.
bird-point: Notoriously windy; avalanche paths and control closures between Indian and Girdwood.
matanuska: Winter glacier travel only with a guide. 4-hour round trip on the icy Glenn Highway; often −20 °C or colder with strong winds.
alyeska-ski: Seward Highway avalanche closures can block access; the upper mountain often goes on wind or visibility holds.
nye-alyeska: Driving back to Anchorage late on New Year's Eve on the Seward Highway is dark and risky: stay in Girdwood or have a sober driver.
snowmachine: Guided backcountry riding: follow the guide's avalanche protocol.
warm-alyeska-nordic-spa: Adults 18+ only; holiday dates sell out.
warm-tolovana-hot-springs: 10+ mi backcountry ski in, remote, extreme cold possible: a serious trip, far beyond the 2-hour range.
